summary: Verified live (Chrome + 12 crawler UAs) and in source. Crawlers are NOT screened: middleware.ts allowlists Googlebot/Bingbot/GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot/ChatGPT-User/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/PerplexityBot/Google-Extended/Applebot first (L150-151, L209-210); all 12 UAs got 200 with full HTML on /, /cities/bend, /subdivisions/ridge-at-eagle-crest, /listing/220222277, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, /robots.txt; only bare curl / empty UA get middleware's 403 (x-bot-screen: bad-ua / empty-ua). Vercel firewall/Attack Challenge state is UNVERIFIED (MCP calls barred mid-task) but no mitigation/challenge header appeared in ~140 responses; vercel.json carries no headers/redirects. robots.txt allows every AI and search bot and points at /sitemap.xml, an index over five children totalling 9,292 URLs (core 205, geo 4,827, listings 3,283, matrix 885, content 92), all 200 today; cold geo.xml took 36 s (no 504). listings.xml is honest: all 3,283 list numbers are Active/AUC/Pending in listing_tile_mv and 0 are out of the Central Oregon city set. Pages are fully server-rendered with valid JSON-LD. The technical drag sits in the programmatic long tail: (1) any made-up area slug under /homes-for-sale/{city}/... renders 200 index,follow self-canonical with a fabricated H1 (5 shapes, 3 cities); (2) sitemapped /subdivisions/* pages return HTTP 500 under 12-concurrent Googlebot-UA bursts (3/12, 1/12; 23/60 in the first sample) and render cold in 2.5-9 s because generateStaticParams is []; (3) those 2,642 plat pages have essentially no crawlable inbound links (0 anchors from /cities/bend, /cities/redmond, neighborhoods, /site-index; 47 on /subdivisions); (4) the indexable plat set is inverted: legal phase plats with junk titles are indexed while marketing-name pages like /subdivisions/ridge-at-eagle-crest are noindex, and 77% of the 1,815 /homes-for-sale/{city}/{plat} twins have zero listings yet are indexable with the same title; (5) listing detail, search and /oregon routes are dynamic (private, no-store, MISS) because they read searchParams/headers(), so revalidate=300 is dead and 64% of sitemap URLs cost 1-5.5 s per crawl; (6) the sitemap submits 105 zip URLs that 404, 30 duplicate locs, at least 6 redirecting URLs and lastmod=now on ~5,900 URLs; (7) unknown slugs under /cities/{city}/*, /types/*, /subdivisions/*, /housing-market/* are 200 soft-404s. All 17 SEO gates are wired but static; none observes production. Long-form notes with every command, path and header: notes.md in this directory.

findings.title: Any made-up area slug under /homes-for-sale/{city}/ renders an indexable page with a fabricated H1
findings.claim: The search route accepts an arbitrary second segment (and any third segment that is a valid preset) and returns HTTP 200, robots index,follow, a self-referencing canonical and an H1/title built from the slug. This is an unbounded indexable URL space and a fabricated place name (§0).
findings.evidence: Five probes, three cities, Chrome UA (soft404-and-dupes.mjs, final curl batch): /homes-for-sale/bend/zzz-not-a-real-area-9x -> 200 index,follow h1 'Zzz Not A Real Area 9x homes for sale'; /homes-for-sale/redmond/totally-made-up-place-42 -> 200 index,follow canonical=self h1 'Totally Made Up Place 42 homes for sale'; /homes-for-sale/la-pine/not-a-place-at-all -> 200 index,follow; /homes-for-sale/bend/qqq-nope/under-500k -> 200 index,follow h1 'Homes Under $500,000 in Qqq Nope'; /homes-for-sale/bend/zzz-not-real/single-family -> 200 index,follow h1 'Single-Family Homes in Zzz Not Real'. middleware.ts L299-309 and L336-352 validate exactly one segment by design; app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx L96-100 notFound()s only an unknown 3-seg preset; lib/seo-routing.ts shouldNoIndexSearchVariant (L28-58) inspects query params only.
findings.why_it_matters: Every stray link, typo, scraper URL or old plat spelling becomes a new indexable 'homes for sale' page. Google's programmatic-quality signal for the whole /homes-for-sale family degrades, crawl budget is spent on nothing, and the site publishes place names that do not exist.
findings.proposed_fix: In app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx, when slug[1] resolves to no known subdivision browse pair, neighborhood, community or preset, return refusal metadata (noindex, honest title, no canonical) exactly as SubdivisionUnavailable does (a notFound() would ship a 200 under app/loading.tsx). Add the resolved-area check to the sitemap's own pair source (getSubdivisionBrowsePairsByCity) so the page and the sitemap share one set. Add a live contract test in the nightly lane: a garbage area slug must render noindex.

findings.title: Sitemapped /subdivisions/* pages return HTTP 500 under crawler-like concurrency and render cold in 2.5-9 s
findings.claim: The 2,642 plat pages in geo.xml are on-demand renders (generateStaticParams []) that take 2.5-9.1 s cold and fail with a Next 500 page when a dozen are requested in parallel, which is how Googlebot crawls a sitemap.
findings.evidence: sitemap-sample-check.mjs (6 concurrent): 23/60 -> 500. retest-500s.json serial: 23/23 -> 200 in 2.5-5.0 s, x-vercel-cache MISS. burst-500.mjs, 12-concurrent, Googlebot UA, previously untouched URLs: 3/12 and 1/12 -> 500 ('500: Internal Server Error.' Next error page, x-vercel-cache MISS, no x-vercel-error header, 6.4-9.8 s), e.g. /subdivisions/awbrey-village-phase-1, /subdivisions/bend-park-first-addition, /subdivisions/high-pointe-phase-1. app/subdivisions/[slug]/page.tsx L280-282 generateStaticParams returns []; L270 revalidate 900; next.config Cache-Control s-maxage=60. generateMetadata L353-358 awaits getIndexableSubdivisions() and getPlatBoundaryCity() outside any withTimeoutFallbackResult guard, unlike the body reads at L376-384/398-408/428-438/458-466. Runtime logs could not be read (MCP barred).
findings.why_it_matters: A 5xx on a submitted URL is dropped from the index and Google reduces crawl rate site-wide when 5xx rates rise. This is the exact family Matt expects to rank on (subdivision search).
findings.proposed_fix: 1) Read the Vercel runtime logs for the 500s and wrap the two unguarded generateMetadata reads in withTimeoutFallbackResult (metadata must never throw). 2) Warm the class: generateStaticParams over getIndexableSubdivisions() (2,642 slugs) or extend /api/cron/warm-sitemaps to pre-render plat pages in batches so crawls hit ISR HITs. 3) Add a nightly live gate that fetches 12 sitemapped plat URLs concurrently with the Googlebot UA and fails on any 5xx.

findings.title: geo.xml submits 105 /zip/* URLs that return 404
findings.claim: The sitemap emits every 5-digit PostalCode with an active listing statewide (115 zips) while the route only serves the 10 CANONICAL_ZIPS and hard-404s the rest, so 105 submitted URLs are 404s.
findings.evidence: sitemap-sample-check.mjs zip family n=115: status {200:10, 404:105}, titles 'Page not found | Ryan Realty, Central Oregon'; app/sitemap.ts L515-539 (fetchAllRows listings.PostalCode, ACTIVE_STATUS_OR); app/zip/[zip]/page.tsx L170-175 dynamicParams=false, generateStaticParams from CANONICAL_ZIPS; app/zip/[zip]/_v3/zip-constants.ts L67. scripts/check-sitemap-resolvable.mjs checks that the family's route file exists, not that params resolve, so it passes.
findings.why_it_matters: 1.1% of the sitemap is submitted 404s; the repo's own comment (app/sitemap.ts L392-394) says submitting 404s poisons the programmatic-page quality signal. Trust in the sitemap drops and crawl budget is wasted.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit only CANONICAL_ZIPS (import the set into app/sitemap.ts, or pull the zip list from app/zip/[zip]/_v3/zip-constants.ts) and add a drift invariant to check-sitemap-resolvable.mjs that the zip family's params equal the route's generateStaticParams set.

findings.title: 2,642 plat pages are orphaned from the crawlable link graph
findings.claim: No city, neighborhood, site-index or neighborhoods page emits a crawlable <a href='/subdivisions/...'> anchor; the /subdivisions directory lists 47 featured plats; so ~2,595 sitemapped plat pages are reachable only from the sitemap or from a listing that happens to sit inside them.
findings.evidence: Raw-HTML anchor counts (soft404-and-dupes.mjs, render-check.log): /subdivisions 47; /cities/bend 0 (741 listing anchors); /cities/redmond 0; /cities/bend/awbrey-butte 0; /cities/bend/old-bend 0; /site-index 0; /neighborhoods 0; listing detail 1; plat pages min 0 / avg 2 / max 8. components/site/v3/V3PlaceIndex.tsx L6-15 documents the identical 2026-09-09 measurement and built PATTERN 9 to fix it; app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx L436-443 now sends plats to the client-only Atlas ('A-Z /subdivisions is the directory'); app/subdivisions/page.tsx uses publishFeaturedPlats (47 links, 6,586 visible chars).
findings.why_it_matters: Pages with no internal links get little PageRank and are crawled rarely; Google treats sitemap-only URLs as low priority. This is why subdivision pages cannot carry the 'search by subdivision' promise regardless of content quality.
findings.proposed_fix: Make /subdivisions a real A-Z directory of every indexable plat grouped by city (all anchors in served HTML, <details> fold as V3PlaceIndex already does), render a V3PlaceIndex of the city's indexable plats on each /cities/{city} page and of the neighborhood's plats on each /cities/{city}/{nb} page, and add a gate that counts served /subdivisions/ anchors on those three page classes against the indexable set.

findings.title: Listing detail, search and /oregon routes are dynamic renders, not ISR, so 64% of sitemap URLs cost 1-5.5 s per crawl
findings.claim: app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx and app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx read searchParams (and headers()) in the page tree, which opts them out of ISR; every crawler fetch is a full DB-backed render served private/no-store. The revalidate=300 those files export, and the gate that pins it, have no runtime effect.
findings.evidence: Googlebot response headers: /listing/220222277 'cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate', x-vercel-cache MISS, no x-nextjs-prerender; same on /homes-for-sale/bend, /homes-for-sale/bend/boulevard, /homes-for-sale/bend/awbrey-butte/acreage, /oregon/medford, /open-houses/bend. Contrast /cities/bend and /communities/tetherow: 'public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=600', x-nextjs-prerender: 1, x-nextjs-stale-time: 300. Source: app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx L266-270 (await searchParams; isNextRouterPrefetch reads headers()), app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx L94 (await searchParams), app/oregon/[city]/page.tsx L150 (force-dynamic). scripts/check-public-isr-ttl.mjs L41-43 pins revalidate 300 on those files. Measured Googlebot TTFB on listing detail 5.5/1.2/2.6/1.6/1.1/3.3/1.5/1.2 s; 40-URL listing sample avg 2.1 s; 40 browse URLs avg 1.5 s. Class in sitemap: 3,283 listing + 2,388 two-seg + 312 three-seg = 5,983 of 9,292.
findings.why_it_matters: Crawl budget is a function of server response time; slow, uncacheable pages get crawled less and refreshed less, which is the listing/price-change freshness the site sells. It also means every scraper request is a database hit.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the request-time reads out of the cacheable tree: read the prefetch signal and query filters in a client island or a Suspense-wrapped leaf so the no-query canonical document is ISR (Next: keep searchParams/headers() out of the page component; render filters client-side from useSearchParams; for the LCP preload decision use a static default). Then change check-public-isr-ttl.mjs into a live assertion in the nightly lane: fetch each class with the Googlebot UA and require x-nextjs-prerender on the canonical URL.

findings.title: 1,815 /homes-for-sale/{city}/{plat} browse URLs: ~77% have zero listings and duplicate the /subdivisions/{plat} page
findings.claim: The sitemap emits a browse URL for every (city, plat) pair with >=3 lifetime listings of any status; most currently show no inventory, ~3.5K chars of copy, robots index, and the same <title> as the plat's /subdivisions page, so each plat competes with itself and the family reads as thin doorway pages.
findings.evidence: sitemap-sample-results.json hfs2: 39 x 200, 30 with 0 listing hrefs (77%); pairs boulevard, cascade-peaks, 1414-awbrey -> identical <title> 'X homes for sale | Ryan Realty, Central Oregon' on /subdivisions/{s} (noindex,follow, 8-11K chars) and /homes-for-sale/bend/{s} (index,follow, 0 listings, ~3.5K chars); avonlea-estates both index,follow; ridge-at-eagle-crest: /subdivisions noindex with 111 listing anchors vs /homes-for-sale/redmond/... index with 9. app/sitemap.ts L386-429 SUBDIVISION_SITEMAP_MIN_LIFETIME_LISTINGS = 3 across all statuses; matrix 3-seg family (gated >=1 active) sampled 20/20 with listings.
findings.why_it_matters: Two indexable URLs per plat with the same head term split ranking signals, and a large set of zero-inventory 'homes for sale' pages is the classic programmatic thin-content pattern that suppresses a whole section.
findings.proposed_fix: One URL per plat: when a plat is in the indexable /subdivisions set, canonicalize the browse URL to it (or drop it from the sitemap); when it is not, keep the browse URL only if it has >=1 active listing or renders real sold history, otherwise noindex. Encode the decision in one function shared by app/sitemap.ts and the search page (as getMatrixCityPresetNoIndex already does for city x preset) and pin it with check-sitemap-inventory-gate.

findings.title: The indexable plat set is inverted: legal phase plats with junk titles are indexed, marketing-name pages are noindex
findings.claim: Indexability requires a GIS polygon plus >=10 lifetime sales, which selects county phase plats (titles carry phase/lot/replat/document numbers) and excludes the umbrella names people search; a plat slug that collides with a city name is also indexed.
findings.evidence: 22/37 sampled sitemapped plat titles carry legal noise: 'Broken Top Phase Ii C Lots 117 Thru 143 homes for sale · Bend, Oregon', 'Rivers Edge Village Phase Xxii Pz 19 0632 homes for sale', '121 West Phases 1 and 2 711 21 000260 Sub homes for sale · Redmond', 'Deschutes River Recreation Homesites Unit 9 Part I Blocks 41 42 And 53', 'Anderson Ranch P U D'. /subdivisions/ridge-at-eagle-crest (111 listing anchors, 33,752 visible chars) is robots noindex,follow and absent from geo.xml; ridge-at-eagle-crest-7/-10/-11/-14 are submitted. /subdivisions/bend is submitted with title 'Bend homes for sale | Ryan Realty, Central Oregon', identical to /cities/bend. app/subdivisions/[slug]/page.tsx L353-366 (noindex: indexableEntry == null), lib/data/subdivisions/subdivision-index.ts L48.
findings.why_it_matters: Titles are the strongest on-page relevance and CTR signal; nobody searches 'phase ii c lots 117 thru 143'. The page that matches the query is the one being hidden.
findings.proposed_fix: Index the marketing/umbrella plat (aggregate its phases: listings, polygon union, sold history) and canonicalize phase plats to it; clean titles through publishPlatDisplayName (strip phase/lot/unit/replat/document tokens, keep them in body copy); exclude plat slugs that equal a city, community or neighborhood slug from the indexable set; pin title shape with check-content-metadata-style rules for the plat class.

findings.title: lastmod is the generation timestamp for ~5,900 sitemap URLs
findings.claim: core, geo and matrix children stamp lastModified: now on every regeneration, so 5,917 URLs claim modification within the hour; only listings.xml carries real timestamps. Under §0 a date with no basis is fabricated, and Google discounts lastmod it finds unreliable.
findings.evidence: geo.xml 4,827 lastmod tags / 13 distinct values; matrix.xml 885 / 1; core.xml 205 / 27; listings.xml 3,283 / 2,940 distinct (2026-02-28 .. 2026-09-22). app/sitemap.ts 'lastModified: now' at L346-348, 366, 380, 426, 443, 461, 534; app/sitemaps/index.xml/route.ts L48 index lastmod = new Date().
findings.why_it_matters: lastmod is the one lever that tells Google which of 9,292 URLs to recrawl first; when it is noise on two thirds of the map, the honest signal on listings is the only thing left and place pages get recrawled on Google's own schedule.
findings.proposed_fix: Omit lastmod where there is no basis (allowed by the protocol) or derive it per URL from data: MV refresh time for browse/plat pages, latest ModificationTimestamp among a place's listings for place pages, published_at for content. Keep listings as is.

findings.title: Unknown slugs under /cities/{city}/*, /types/*, /subdivisions/*, /housing-market/* are 200 soft-404s
findings.claim: Because every route streams under app/loading.tsx, notFound() thrown in the page body ships HTTP 200 (noindex, 'Page not found', no <h1>); only communities, one-segment cities/open-houses/homes-for-sale, blog index paths and /dev are validated at the edge.
findings.evidence: soft404-and-dupes.mjs: /cities/bend/zzz-not-a-real-neighborhood, /cities/bend/types/condo, /cities/bend/types/zzz, /communities/tetherow/types/condo, /housing-market/zzz-nope -> 200, robots noindex,follow, title 'Page not found', h1 []; /subdivisions/zzz-not-a-real-plat-9x -> 200 noindex 'No subdivision at this address'; /listing/999999999 -> 200 noindex. Real 404s: /zip/97501, /schools/zzz. middleware.ts L252-260 and L294-297 describe the mechanism; app/cities/[slug]/types/[type]/page.tsx L86/L119 notFound().
findings.why_it_matters: Search Console files these as soft 404s, which count against site quality and spend crawl budget; the noindex only limits indexing, not the crawl cost or the signal.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate at the edge where the set is static (type slugs are a fixed spec list; neighborhoods can be a committed JSON generated by a gate from the neighborhoods table) and return a real 404 from middleware, as isInvalidGeoSlug does; for plats and listings keep the refusal page but add x-robots-tag noindex and consider removing the root loading boundary from place routes so notFound() can set 404.

findings.title: /cities/{city} documents are 1.7-3.8 MB of HTML with the Atlas geometry inlined
findings.claim: The city page ships its map polygons and hundreds of listing cards in the HTML/RSC payload; /cities/bend is 3.77 MB, most of it one 1.3 MB Atlas chunk with 22,005 inline coordinate tokens. Core Web Vitals were not measured here (ux-live reader), but this is the document every crawler and visitor must download and parse for the site's most important hub.
findings.evidence: nav-and-size.mjs: /cities/bend html 3,770,815 B; RSC 2,056,864 B in 105 chunks; largest chunk 1,305,887 B begins '"className":"place-one-map"'; 22,005 longitude-like tokens; 741 listing anchors; 787 ; non-script HTML 1,687,173 B. /cities/bend/awbrey-butte 2,011,117 B; /cities/bend/types/single-family 1,683,632 B (render-check.log). app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx L406 builds AtlasRegion with inline geometry.
findings.why_it_matters: Page weight of this size hurts LCP/INP on mobile and slows Googlebot's render; Google's page-quality systems and the mobile-first index both read the rendered page.
findings.proposed_fix: Serve Atlas geometry from a cached JSON endpoint (or simplified polygons) fetched client-side, cap served listing cards to the first fold plus a crawlable index, and add a gate on served HTML bytes per public class.

findings.title: Sitemap hygiene: 30 duplicate locs and at least 6 redirecting URLs
findings.claim: core.xml lists /cities, /homes-for-sale and /open-houses twice for the 10 seeded cities, and geo.xml includes plat/browse URLs that middleware or next.config redirect.
findings.evidence: grep '<loc>' sitemap-core.xml | sort | uniq -d -> 30 (e.g. /cities/bend, /cities/redmond ... x2); app/sitemap.ts L251-257 static seed and L343-349 dynamic loop both push them. hops.ts over all 9,292 URLs: 5 /subdivisions/* resolve through resolvePreRenderHop (brasada-ranch, eagle-crest, mountain-high -> /communities/*; first-on-the-hill-sites -> /subdivisions/1st-on-the-hillsites); live /homes-for-sale/bend/awbrey-butte -> 301 /cities/bend/awbrey-butte (1 of 40 sampled browse URLs).
findings.why_it_matters: Small, but each is a wasted fetch and a 'submitted URL redirects' warning that erodes trust in the map.
findings.proposed_fix: Dedupe by URL at the end of buildAllUrls and run every emitted path through resolvePreRenderHop / the geo-city rules before emit (pure, Edge-safe functions already exist); pin both in check-sitemap-resolvable.

findings.title: Property-type pages are indexable but absent from every sitemap and from the nav
findings.claim: /cities/{city}/types/{type} and /communities/{c}/types/{type} render index,follow with query-shaped titles but are linked only from the parent city page and sibling type pages, and no sitemap child contains a /types/ URL.
findings.evidence: render-check.log /cities/bend/types/single-family -> 200 index,follow title '757 single-family homes for sale in Bend, Oregon'; grep -c '/types/' over sitemap-{core,geo,listings,matrix,content}.xml -> 0 each; header/footer hrefs (nav-and-size.mjs) contain no /types/ link; /cities/bend links 10 type pages.
findings.why_it_matters: These are exactly the 'property type' queries Matt expects to win; discovery depends on one link per city page.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit the type family in app/sitemap.ts (declare it in check-sitemap-resolvable), and add the type doors to the city mega-menu or footer.

findings.title: SEO gates are all static; the live defects above pass every one of them
findings.claim: All 17 SEO/sitemap/ISR gates inspect source text or ASTs, so a route that is dynamic at runtime (SEO-5), a sitemap family whose params 404 (SEO-3), pages that 500 under load (SEO-2) and phantom indexable pages (SEO-1) all ship green; check-public-isr-ttl even pins a TTL constant on routes where it cannot apply.
findings.evidence: package.json ci:gates:chain contains all 17 (list in notes.md §11); scripts/check-public-isr-ttl.mjs L10 and L41-43 pin 300 on app/search/page.tsx, app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx, app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx while live headers show private, no-store; scripts/check-sitemap-resolvable.mjs header: 'STATIC gate (no DB, no network)'.
findings.why_it_matters: THE LOOP's 'lock behind a gate' step cannot hold runtime behaviour if no gate observes production; the same class of regression will recur.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one nightly-lane live gate (Googlebot UA, ignoreHTTPSErrors) that samples each sitemap family and asserts: status 200, x-nextjs-prerender on canonical URLs of cacheable classes, no 5xx at concurrency 10, params resolve for zip/type families, and garbage area slugs render noindex.
